messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT created: High pod churn in serving-runtime (tokenizer stage) — several CPU OOMs and container kills observed. Trigger: kubelet OOMKilled events across model-serving pods.
oncall-bot: Pager sent to maya, alex (oncall) and ryan (runtime).
maya: I'm on it. seeing lots of `SIGKILL` from OOM on pods running `tokenizer-worker`. 5xx and client retries spiking on hosted API routes.
alex: Confirmed — metric spike around 08:12 UTC. CPU usage on tokenizer containers climbs to 98% then kubelet kills them.
ryan: Any recent deploys?
maya: No deploys in the last 6h. Rolling restarts started after the first pod died, which made more requests hit same nodes.
sara: I'm looking at logs — tokenization of a few long prompts is blowing memory. Example log: ```
2026-02-23T08:11:58Z tokenizer-worker[pid=2143]: Allocating 2.4G for token buffer
2026-02-23T08:12:00Z kubelet: Container runtime: killed process 2143 (python) total-vm:3100000kB, anon-rss:2900000kB
```
maya: Repro steps local-ish: send a prompt with 150k characters triggers a huge tensor in single-threaded tokenizer. It seems we don't chunk long user inputs in the preproc.
alex: Checking K8s events: many nodes with kubelet out-of-memory for user pods, some node flapping reported.
ops-bot: Node 10.23.4.12 marked NotReady for 2m due to kernel OOM.
ryan: Immediate mitigation suggestion: reduce tokenizer parallelism and add a hard limit on input size at the edge. Can we patch the gateway to 1) reject inputs > 100k chars with 400, 2) inject a tokenization chunker env var to tokenizer pods?
maya: I can push a config override to the deployment to set TOKENIZER_MAX_CHARS=100000 and TOKENIZER_WORKERS=1. Will roll canary to 2 pods then scale.
sara: Also enabling request-level circuit-breaker for heavy tails: route heavy prompts to the cheaper/buffer queue.
alex: Who can do the rolling restart? I'm on infra, I can queue it — but want to avoid thrashing nodes. Recommend cordon nodes with repeated OOMs and drain one at a time to rebalance.
ops-bot: Node 10.23.4.12 cordoned by alex.
maya: Pushing config now. Command I used: ```kubectl set env deployment/tokenizer TOKENIZER_MAX_CHARS=100000 TOKENIZER_WORKERS=1 -n serving && kubectl rollout status deploy/tokenizer -n serving```
maya: Canary applied to 2 pods. Watching metrics.
ryan: On logs I see the tokenizer process uses a single large allocation during regex-based normalization — we'll need a safer streaming tokenizer in the code path. I'll open a quick PR to add chunked processing with streaming iterators, but that's post-mitigation.
sara: Customer impact: Hosted API errors rose to ~14% 5xx for 10m window. Affected customers: a handful of high-throughput tenants — emailed SRE runbook owners.
maya: After canary, CPU spikes dropped and no further OOM kills on canary pods in the last 4m. Throughput recovered to baseline with small retry backlog.
alex: Rolling the rest with the same env now, doing 1 pod at a time to avoid surge.
ops-bot: Rolling restart started at 08:22 UTC.
ryan: Quick mitigation checklist (for the postmortem): 1) add input size validation at edge (gateway) 2) add tokenizer streaming/chunking to avoid OOM 3) add per-pod cpu oom_score_adj or cgroups throttles 4) increase observability on tokenizer memory allocations 5) add a bench test with long prompts.
sara: I'll update incident page and notify customer support with impact numbers and mitigation steps.
maya: Handing off to night oncall (alex) at 08:30 UTC. If we see reoccurrence, escalate to infra and consider node replacement.
alex: Taking handoff, will monitor for 2h. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident updated: Severity set to P2. Linked runbook: /runbooks/tokenizer_oom.md (internal).
ryan: Follow-up action: I'll post PR link and estimate for code fix in the postmortem.
maya: Postmortem owner assigned: maya. ETA for postmortem draft: 48h.
sara: Closing this thread once the postmortem link is added and customer-notifications are complete. :eyes:
